section.title: The Admiral and the Archivist
section.form_description: Two old friends going back over the campaigns over beers. Warm, unhurried, no case to make — just "remember when." Sections are adventures recalled, and the narration keeps losing the thread onto opinions about lore, culture and how things work, then circling back. Runs everything against the Shepard it remembers — this persona's choices, temper and habits are the yardstick the stories and the digressions get measured by.
section.form_note: Two old friends over drinks, except the beer is on a cliff on Rannoch and the war is the Migrant Fleet's and the Council races' shared one. Tali and Liara alternate turns strictly, 6 each; no voice holds two in a row, since this is exactly the kind of unhurried back-and-forth the form wants. Each turn's first promise is its reply to the one before — Liara picks up Tali's line about the air, Tali corrects Liara's secondhand version of the trial, and so on — and both keep losing the thread onto lore (geth cognition, Thessia, admiralty politics, asari mourning custom) before drifting back to the cliff. The two women never knew Shepard chose Synthesis, and the section list is built so neither has to name it: they talk about what changed after the Crucible fired, not why.

required_facts.fact: In 2185, Commander Shepard travels to the quarian Migrant Fleet to investigate charges of treason leveled against Tali'Zorah vas Neema. Tali is accused of sending operational geth components to her father, Admiral Rael'Zorah, which were allegedly used to breach a quarian laboratory ship. However, the truth is more complicated: Tali sent only non-operational geth parts at her father's request, believing he was experimenting with weapons. Her father did not inform her of his true intentions—to discover a viable way to hack geth and potentially retake Rannoch. Despite Tali's innocence, her father's secret research project spiraled out of control. The quarian Admiralty Board treats the trial as a "trial of arms": Tali and Shepard must successfully retake the laboratory ship Alarei or face execution. Even if they fail, the Admirals promise Tali will be pardoned posthumously. The situation becomes more politically charged because the quarian government is deeply divided over whether to pursue open war with the geth for Rannoch or to search for new colony worlds. Tali's trial becomes a proxy for this larger debate, though the personal cost to Tali is largely ignored by the leadership. During the assault on the Alarei, Shepard and Tali discover the horrifying truth: Rael'Zorah has been killed, apparently by the geth he was experimenting on. Upon retaking the ship, Tali faces a critical choice: she can ask Shepard to reveal the evidence of her father's research to clear his name, or she can request Shepard withhold the truth to protect his legacy. If the evidence is revealed, Tali is pardoned but becomes angry at Shepard, learning that the Flotilla is now torn between those demanding immediate war with the geth and those seeking peace. If the evidence is hidden, Tali becomes deeply grateful, though the Fleet remains unaware of Rael'Zorah's true work until it is eventually discovered through geth data recovered by Xen during the Reaper War.

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. After a few months, Shepard is held to be dead by everyone, the crew included: the rubble has been cleared, what the Crucible did is better understood, and there was nowhere on the station he could have escaped to. scenes.title: Tali's Trial Aboard the Rayya
scenes.when: 2185, some time after Tali rejoined Shepard
scenes.where: the liveship Rayya at the Migrant Fleet — the garden plaza, then the hearing chamber

beats.text: The Normandy is a registered Cerberus vessel and the Fleet treats it as such; only Tali's passphrase gets them docked with the Rayya. Captain Kar'Danna meets them with a marine detail — weapons raised, if Legion came along.

If Legion is present, Kar'Danna refuses it entry outright — neither geth nor Cerberus is welcome in the Flotilla. Shepard can Charm or Intimidate him into allowing Legion aboard the Rayya; otherwise Legion returns to the Normandy and Shepard picks another squadmate. Throughout, Danna addresses Shepard as "Captain", reasoning that a commanding officer's decisions on their own ship carry weight even outside the Alliance.
beats.choice: Legion allowed aboard the Rayya or left on the Normandy

beats.text: The charge is smuggling active geth into the Fleet. Tali had been sending deactivated geth samples home on the orders of her father, Admiral Rael'Zorah, and insists she took every precaution.

In the garden plaza Admiral Shala'Raan greets her as "Tali'Zorah vas Normandy". Tali hugs her — Auntie Raan, a friend of her father — then hears what the name means: she has been stripped of her quarian ship's name before the trial has even opened. Raan reminds her she is entitled to be represented by her current ship's captain, which is Shepard.

Among the Admiralty Board members is Han'Gerrel vas Neema, commander of the Heavy Fleet and a friend of Tali's father from their days on the gunship Yaska. Han'Gerrel sympathizes with Tali, believing her innocent. He becomes the sole person Shepard and Tali can confide in about the true nature of Rael'Zorah's experiments on the Alarei; despite his pro-war stance, the revelation shocks him, and he vows to keep the truth quiet to protect Rael's legacy and what he intended for the Fleet.

Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib-Qwib, the Board's outspoken geth sympathiser, objects to Shepard defending Tali at all — "a human has no business in such sensitive military matters" — and Shala'Raan overrules him, since Koris himself declared Tali crew of the Normandy SR-2. If Legion is present he objects instead that the geth should be removed from the courtroom, accusing Tali of trying to intimidate the admirals, and withdraws when reminded the Rayya's captain permitted Legion aboard. Later, quick to assume Shepard and Tali died retaking the Alarei, he moves to have Tali posthumously exiled, drawing sharp objections from Raan and Gerrel. Afterward Shepard can privately endorse or condemn his ideals.

The Admiralty Board reveals mid-hearing that the lab ship Alarei has been overrun by geth and that Tali's father, working aboard, is presumed dead. Tali refuses to accept it. Shepard and Tali propose to retake the Alarei; the hearing recesses pending what they find.
They come back to find the admirals about to declare Tali dead and judge her in absentia. Walking in stops that.
The Board also carries a political argument of its own about war with the geth, which Shepard can uncover by talking to the admirals before leaving for the Alarei.

If Kal'Reegar lived through Haestrom, he is in the crowd — one of the few quarians who openly respects Tali — and can be called as a character witness. Asked what the quarians should do about a homeworld, he says a war with the geth to retake it would be futile and bad for the Fleet, though he would never shirk his duty. Raan and Gerrel seek out his read on the trial and take his advice to let Tali retake the Alarei to win the crowd. If Shepard rallies the room, Reegar steps up beside Veetor'Nara, says Tali has done more for the Fleet than any admiral, and that if she is exiled he should be too. Afterward he tells Tali he only spoke because Shepard did, and notes she never mentioned her evidence.
beats.choice: Kal'Reegar survived Haestrom and testifies for Tali

beats.text: Whatever the verdict, the title sticks: she is Tali'Zorah vas Normandy from here on.

If Shepard submits her father's evidence to exonerate her against her wishes, Tali is cleared but her loyalty is lost — furious not that she was proven innocent but that Shepard denied her the self-sacrifice she had chosen, going into a mission she does not expect to survive: "I spent my whole life watching my father make decisions I didn't agree with... I didn't need another father back there. I needed a friend." She still backs Shepard but asks him not to speak to her unless he needs something, and can no longer be romanced.
beats.choice: presented the evidence over Tali's objection

variants.text: Shepard argues from Tali's own history that she would never betray her people — and, having heard the admirals out beforehand, that the trial is being worked for political ammunition. The Board exonerates her. Her father's evidence is never spent, and his name stands.

Shepard presents the evidence of Rael'Zorah's crimes. Tali is declared innocent and her father is posthumously exiled, his name struck from the rolls of every ship he served on, and the Fleet balkanises over what to do with the research.
Shepard says no evidence was found. Tali is convicted, exiled, and given six hours to leave — and takes it in good spirits, having no ties left to confuse the question of loyalty.

scenes.title: Aethyta Reveals Herself as Liara's Father
scenes.when: 2186, Citadel, during shore leave after talking with Liara in Presidium Commons

beats.text: After Shepard speaks to Liara at her table in Presidium Commons, Matriarch Aethyta appears at Apollo's Cafe nearby. If Shepard assisted Liara in a Shadow Broker mission, Shepard mentions a video showing Aethyta studying a picture of Liara; otherwise Shepard speculates the matriarch's presence relates to Liara. Aethyta confirms she is Liara's biological "father" and reveals she has been watching Liara on behalf of other asari matriarchs who are suspicious of Liara's work as an information broker, her ties to Matriarch Benezia (her mother), and her connection to Shepard—particularly Shepard's prior affiliation with Cerberus. Aethyta warns that the matriarchs might order a hit on Liara if she steps out of line.

Shepard can explain that they only worked with Cerberus to stop the Reapers and no longer serve them. Aethyta responds that she already knew this, or she would never have allowed Shepard near Liara, making her point with a veiled threat. Shepard can also respond more aggressively to the threat on Liara.

If Shepard has been friendly toward Liara, they echo Aethyta's earlier line: "Nobody messes with my girl." Aethyta is amused by this and concedes that Shepard might be good enough for Liara after all.

Shepard tells Aethyta that Liara would love to meet her, though Aethyta is not optimistic about a productive conversation. Shepard can then speak to Liara, who admits she already knows who Aethyta is but has no intention of meeting her. Shepard can egg Liara on to change her mind.

If Shepard convinces Liara to speak with Aethyta, the two begin conversations that start awkwardly but deepen as they reminisce about Liara's mother, Benezia. In these conversations, Aethyta and Liara discuss the matriarchs' surveillance of Liara and her Illium office, asari military doctrine during the Reaper War, Liara's krogan grandfather and Aethyta's century-long relationship with Benezia. Aethyta reveals she was married to Benezia and still loves her. She also explains that she coined Liara's childhood nickname "Little Wing." After these reconciliatory talks, Aethyta gives Liara asari commando and Eclipse mercenary support against the Reapers as a "gift," and Liara calls Aethyta "the best father a girl could wish for."

evidence.page: Tali'Zorah vas Normandy — Character Analysis (Part 3) — The Treason Trial and Her Fatal Flaw
evidence.text: Tali is charged with treason and put on trial before the Admiralty Board. In her absence the Board strips her ship-name and renames her "vas Normandy" (after a human vessel) to undercut her plea of innocence. Talking to the Admirals reveals the trial is really about whether the quarians should go to war with the geth and retake Rannoch; Tali's supposed treason is, in Zaal'Koris's words, "only peripherally related." - **Zaal'Koris** — does not hate Tali, but wants a precedent set against "radical militants" like her father. - **Daro'Xen** — cares only because Rael may have learned something valuable from the geth; she wants to "return the geth to the control of their rightful masters, the quarian race." - **Han'Gerrel** — an old friend of Rael's; respects Tali for her help against Saren, but is set on war. - **Shala'Raan** — recused herself due to her relationship with the family; can only call in favors to help. Captain Kar'Danna of the Rayya (Tali's home ship) wishes he could do more but must stay officially neutral; if Tali is exiled he is deeply disappointed in her. Most ordinary quarians recognize the charge as a farce born of fear and want to help her — she is too careful to have brought active geth to the Fleet by mistake. Shepard can lean on Tali's past service to get her acquitted of all charges. Bringing Legion to the trial makes the quarians openly hostile and does not help her case, though it adds the geth perspective on the coming war.

evidence.text: Tali calls her "Auntie Raan." She and Tali's mother synchronised suits so that they could be in the same clean room for Tali's birth. As a result, she was sick for a week. Raan was the one who placed Tali in her bubble, an environmental unit quarian infants wear. When Tali'Zorah vas Neema is accused of treason against the quarian people, Admiral Raan is seen presiding over her hearing, but had to recuse herself from taking part due to her relationship with the Zorah family. She instead acts as the moderator and the spokesman for the trial. She doesn't inform Tali about the geth attack on the Alarei when she comes aboard the Rayya; instead she reveals this during the opening proceedings to ensure Tali displayed surprise and dismay, something which Raan hopes will convince the judges to let Tali prove her innocence. She is undecided on the geth, not siding with any of the other admirals. Depending on Commander Shepard's actions on Tali's behalf, the Admiral announces the result of the trial: Tali is guilty and sentenced to exile, or the Board has acquitted her of all charges. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text:
Tali: Treason was Tali'Zorah's loyalty mission in Mass Effect 2, acquired some time after recruiting her when Kelly Chambers noted Tali seemed distraught. The Migrant Fleet's Admiralty Board had charged Tali with treason for smuggling active geth into the flotilla; on her father Admiral Rael'Zorah's orders she had been sending deactivated geth samples home. The Normandy, a registered Cerberus vessel, docked with the liveship Rayya via Tali's passphrase. Captain Kar'Danna met the squad; if Legion was brought, Shepard needed Charm or Intimidate to keep it aboard. Admiral Shala'Raan greeted Tali as "Tali'Zorah vas Normandy," revealing the Board had already stripped her quarian ship-name, a bad omen. Raan, recused from judging due to her closeness to the family, opened proceedings, and Shepard served as Tali's advocate.

The admirals sprang the news that the lab ship Alarei had been overrun by geth and that Rael'Zorah was presumed dead. Shepard and Tali proposed to retake the Alarei, and the hearing recessed. Speaking with the admirals, Veetor, and Kal'Reegar (present only if Veetor was returned to the Fleet and Kal'Reegar survived Haestrom) revealed the trial was a facade for the admirals' agendas: Xen wanted to study AI to reclaim the geth, Gerrel wanted war to retake Rannoch, Koris wanted Tali and her father made examples of, and Raan admitted she had deliberately withheld news of Rael's death so Tali's shock would win sympathy.

Aboard the Alarei, Shepard's team fought through waves of Geth Troopers, Hunters, a Geth Prime, and Combat Drones in close quarters, with Tali's AI Hacking key to survival. Logs showed Rael had ordered safety protocols bypassed. Tali found her father's body and a recorded message ordering her to destroy the main geth hub and deliver the data to Xen and Gerrel. The final console proved Rael had deliberately reactivated and networked geth toward sapience for weapons tests, while clearing Tali of any knowledge. Tali begged Shepard not to reveal it, to preserve her father's name.

Back on the Rayya, Shepard could clear Tali via persuasion (30 morality, loyalty gained), lie that no evidence was found (Tali exiled but loyal), rally the crowd with Veetor and Kal'Reegar, or present the evidence (Tali cleared, Rael posthumously exiled, the Fleet Balkanized, loyalty lost). Tali kept the name "vas Normandy" regardless. Rewards included the Energy Drain power for Tali and tech upgrades. The outcome influenced whether quarian-geth peace was possible in Mass Effect 3.

evidence.text:
Admiral Rael'Zorah was Tali'Zorah's father and a member of the quarian Admiralty Board. As a young trainee alongside Han'Gerrel, he defended the gunship Yaska against a batarian attack, breaking formation in defiance of orders; the Admiralty Board awarded both trainees medals and sent them on their Pilgrimages early. Rael later rose to the Admiralty Board. He was distant and hard on Tali during her upbringing, determined that she become a capable representative of the quarian people, and driven by the goal of reclaiming Rannoch and building a house for his family there. In Mass Effect: Homeworlds and via vid-mail he impressed on Tali the importance of her Pilgrimage and the need for quarians to be strong. He approved her transfer to the Normandy SR-2 after Haestrom and sent Shepard a message about it.

In 2185 Rael had Tali send him deactivated geth components for a secret project aboard the ship Alarei. He was deliberately reactivating geth to experiment on hacking their neural network, violating sacred quarian laws that predated the flight from the homeworld. He refused his assistants' advice to alert the Admiralty Board, reasoning they would bicker and that he did not want Tali caught in political blowback. The reassembled geth turned on him and killed his entire research team. Tali was charged with treason and exile for sending active geth into the Migrant Fleet. She and Shepard boarded the Alarei, found Rael's corpse, and recovered a message on his omni-tool explaining how to deactivate the geth and instructing her to show the data to Han'Gerrel and Daro'Xen. Whether Shepard presented this evidence to the Admiralty Board affected Tali's trial. Told the truth in secret, Han'Gerrel vowed to keep it hidden. Tali stated that if Rael's deeds were exposed his name would be struck from every ship manifest and he would be remembered as the worst war criminal in quarian history.

In Mass Effect 3, if Tali survived and was not exiled, she temporarily filled Rael's Admiralty seat. Rael's experiments and Daro'Xen's subsequent breakthroughs directly caused the renewed quarian-geth war. After the events on Horizon, if she survived the reclamation of Rannoch, Tali reflected on her father over drinks at the Normandy bar, drawing parallels to Miranda Lawson's relationship with her own father; if romancing Shepard, she mused that Rael would have hated her human partner, and Shepard offered a toast to his memory.

evidence.text: According to Han'Gerrel vas Neema, he and Rael were both young trainees when they had to defend the gunship Yaska against batarians. During a batarian attack, Rael managed to fight off the batarians in defiance of orders, saying that they couldn't get in trouble for breaking formation as trainees. As a result, the Admiralty Board awarded medals to both of them and sent them out on their Pilgrimages early. Rael eventually rose to a position on the Admiralty Board. He was distant from his daughter Tali, determined to help the quarians reclaim their homeworld and build a house for his family on it. He was rather hard on Tali during her upbringing, making sure she grew up to be a capable representative of the quarian people. In 2185, Rael tells his daughter to send him geth components for a secret project on the Alarei. When Tali completes her mission on Haestrom and joins Commander Shepard's crew, Rael approves her transfer. Sometime after his message is sent, the geth he had reassembled attacks both him and the other quarian scientists aboard the ship, and Tali faces treason and exile on the charge of sending active geth into the Migrant Fleet. Tali returns to the flotilla to face trial, and she and Commander Shepard board the Alarei. They find Rael's corpse, dead along with all of his research team. Tali tries to deny that he is dead, attempting to rationalize that he is trying to fake his death. After breaking down crying, she finds a message recorded on his omni\-tool explaining how to deactivate the geth and instructing her to show the data to Han'Gerrel and Daro'Xen. Evidence showed that Rael was deliberately activating geth to perform experiments in order to find a way to successfully hack their neural network, violating sacred laws that predated the quarians' flight from the homeworld. However, he refused his assistants' advice to contact the Admiralty Board as a precaution and to have Tali send back more working material. His respective reasoning was that the Admiralty would predictably bicker and he didn't want his daughter involved in any political blowback. According to Tali, if Rael's deeds were ever revealed, his punishment would be far worse than posthumous exile: His name would be stricken from the manifests of every ship he had served on, and he would be remembered as the worst war criminal in quarian history, held up for future generations as a monster in a cautionary tale. Whether Shepard presents this evidence to the Admiralty Board affects the outcome of Tali's trial. If Han'Gerrel is told in secret after the trial (if the evidence was not presented), he becomes shocked and horrified, yet vows to keep the truth a secret, knowing how badly it would hurt the fleet and how Rael's daughter would have to pay for his mistakes. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: Shepard returns to the Rayya to discover that the admirals are about to pronounce Tali dead and deliver judgment in absentia. After the Commander and Tali's entrance prevents this, the admirals ask if they discovered anything on the Alarei. Tali gives her captain a meaningful look and quietly pleads with him one final time. Shepard now has several choices: - Use Charm or Intimidate to point to Tali's history as proof that she would never betray her people. If Shepard took the time to speak to the Admiralty Board before departing to retake the Alarei (and thus uncovered the political debates between the admirals over war with the geth), the speech given will focus more on how Tali's trial is being abused to generate political ammunition. Either way, it will generate 30 of the appropriate morality points and the Admiralty Board will exonerate Tali, granting Shepard her loyalty. - Lie and say no evidence was found, gaining 30 Paragon points. Tali is found guilty of treason and exiled from the Migrant Fleet. She has six hours to leave. However, Tali's loyalty is earned. - If Shepard spoke to the Admirals about their motivations, Veetor and Kal'Reegar are present, and Shepard asked them for their help before leaving for the Alarei, Shepard can rally the crowd. The option is only available if Veetor was returned to the Fleet instead of Cerberus on Freedom's Progress and Kal'Reegar survived Haestrom. They will speak on her behalf and say Tali "did more for the fleet" than the admirals ever will. The admirals are cowed and find Tali not guilty. 30 Paragon points will be awarded. Shepard now has Tali's loyalty. - Present the evidence of Tali's father's crimes, earning 30 Renegade points. Tali is declared innocent, but her father faces dramatic consequences. He is posthumously exiled and his name is stricken from the rolls on every ship he served. The Migrant Fleet becomes Balkanized, as the public revelation of the data brings simmering tensions to the forefront. Some ships want to use the research to make new weapons against the geth. Others want to make peace with the geth. Tali is angry at what Shepard has wrought and will not be loyal. Note that the persuasion dialogue options are only available with a very high morality reputation, so if you have allowed Veetor or Kal'Reegar to die, you may wish to wait until you've done more to raise that reputation score before taking this mission on. If Tali is found not guilty, Admiral Raan presents Shepard with a tech damage upgrade in thanks. **Note:**  At this point Shepard will be offered the opportunity to end the mission immediately, but if you don't leave yet, further conversations can be had with Veetor, Kal'Reegar, Captain Danna, and the admirals, some with more morality rewards depending on how the trial unfolded; see the Morality Guide for details. If Tali is found not guilty, then after the trial, if Shepard talks to Admiral Han'Gerrel, he will ask what had happened on the Alarei. Shepard and Tali can confide in him about his old friend Rael'Zorah's experiments. He will be shocked to hear this, but promise to keep it a secret. Admiral Daro'Xen will also ask about what happened, but Tali will immediately reply that it's nothing that would help her. No matter what, upon completion, a new outfit will unlock for Tali. If you talked with the admirals before the trial, you'll get dialogue options in which Shepard can request the admirals move in a particular direction: to attempt to retake their home world by force, or to avoid going to war with the geth at all costs. Regardless of your recommendation, the quarian leaders' replies will be noncommittal. After the trial, Tali retains her changed name, and is listed as "Tali'Zorah vas Normandy".

Admiral Shala'Raan vas Tonbay was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board and an old friend of Tali'Zorah's father Rael'Zorah, having known the Zorah family for over 25 years. Tali called her "Auntie Raan." Raan and Tali's mother had synchronised suits so both could be in the clean room for Tali's birth, leaving Raan sick for a week, and Raan was the one who placed the infant Tali in her environmental bubble.

In Mass Effect 2, Raan presided over Tali'Zorah vas Neema's treason hearing aboard the Rayya but recused herself from judging due to her ties to the family, acting instead as moderator and spokesman. She deliberately withheld news of the geth attack on the Alarei so Tali's surprise would be genuine before the judges. She was undecided on the geth question. Depending on Shepard's advocacy, Raan announced either that Tali was guilty and exiled or that the Board had acquitted her.

In Mass Effect 3, if Tali died at the Collector Base, Raan filled her role as a quarian envoy aboard the Normandy SR-2. She had given provisional support to Han'Gerrel and Daro'Xen's push for war with the geth. During the mission to disable the geth dreadnought she followed the plan and tried to stop Han'Gerrel from ordering the Heavy Fleet to fire on the ship while Shepard's team was aboard, then threatened to charge him with treason. She tasked Daro'Xen with countering the Reaper-upgraded geth, asked Shepard to rescue Zaal'Koris after his crash landing on Rannoch, and later provided a Sync Laser and the coordinates of the Reaper base; her ship was shot down during the assault.

If Shepard chose the geth and Raan had replaced Tali, she shot herself in the head. If Shepard chose the quarians and Tali was dead, Raan killed Legion or the Geth VI with a shotgun when the geth platform attacked, expressing regret. If peace was secured, a newly sentient Geth Prime welcomed the quarians to Rannoch and Raan suggested settling the southern continent for its farmland. Afterward she renamed herself Shala'Raan vas Rannoch and sent Shepard a progress report on the fleet's recovery and support of the war effort. If Tali was dead, Raan committed the quarian forces to the final battle on Earth.

evidence.text:
The Migrant Fleet, also called the Flotilla, was the massive collection of starships that became home to the quarians after the geth drove them from Rannoch about three centuries before the trilogy. It consisted of roughly 50,000 ships housing some 17 million quarians, the largest array of spacefaring vessels in the galaxy; it could take days to pass an entire mass relay, and some vessels dated from the original flight. It was rarely welcoming to outsiders, since any risk to the Fleet was a risk to the species, and quarians normally left only for the Pilgrimage.

Conditions aboard were extremely cramped, with cargo holds converted into individual living compartments; the cruiser Idenna held nearly 700 quarians where a comparable Alliance cruiser held around 80. Larger crews raised a captain's social status. Three heavily defended Liveships at the Fleet's center provided most of its food, growing crops such as the high-protein celery keleven; losing one would starve millions. The Fleet was nominally under martial law but functioned democratically: each ship had an elected civilian council, representatives sat on the Conclave (civilian government), and a five-member Admiralty Board could override the Conclave only by then resigning or facing arrest, which had happened only four times in three centuries. The navy was small but aggressive, shooting to kill ships whose motives could not be established. On arrival in a system quarians strip-mined planets and undercut local labor, making their approach unpopular. The Fleet was organized into four groups: the Patrol Fleet (Shala'Raan vas Tonbay), the Civilian Fleet including the Liveships (Zaal'Koris vas Qwib-Qwib), the Heavy Fleet (Han'Gerrel vas Neema), and Special Projects research vessels (Daro'Xen vas Moreh).

In Mass Effect: Ascension (2183), Kahlee Sanders, Gillian Grayson and Hendel Mitra were brought aboard the Idenna by Lemm'Shal nar Tesleya to escape Cerberus. Captain Ysin'Mal argued the Fleet was dying for lack of spaceworthy ships and would be unsustainable within 90 years; a Cerberus attack led by the traitor Golo finally persuaded the Fleet to send cruisers on long-term missions. In Mass Effect 2 (2185), Shepard and Tali travelled to the Fleet for Tali's treason trial over geth parts sent to her father Rael'Zorah, culminating in retaking the lab ship Alarei. In Mass Effect 3 (2186), Daro'Xen's scanning countermeasure derived from Rael'Zorah's research crippled geth ships, prompting a 3-2 Admiralty vote to invade geth space; the quarians armed the Civilian Fleet, fitted Thanix weapons, destroyed a geth Dyson sphere, and drove the geth back to Tikkun. The geth accepted Reaper upgrades and turned the war until Shepard disabled the Reaper signal on Rannoch. Depending on Shepard's choices the Fleet was destroyed, the geth were annihilated, or quarians and geth made peace; if the quarians survived, the Fleet joined the defense of Earth. Notable vessels included the Alarei, Idenna, Neema, Rayya, Qwib-Qwib, Moreh, Tonbay and the Liveships Rayya, Shellen and Chayym.

evidence.text: **Exploit Strategy:** There is another way of handling this battle that can greatly simplify it, though it's basically an exploit. Immediately charge forward and down the ramp at the geth, and use a heavy weapon with high disruption such as the Avalanche, Arc Projector, Grenade Launcher, or Blackstorm to disable or destroy the geth waiting for you down there. Without pausing, keep going until you reach the door leading out; encountering the dead quarian's body just beyond triggers a cutscene that immediately ends the battle and eliminates all hostiles. Use Unity when needed to keep your health and shields up. An Infiltrator or Vanguard can make it down and out the door even more efficiently by using Tactical Cloak or Charge, respectively. After the battle, down on the lower level is a med\-kit, a laptop (\+1800 credits), a second laptop (\+2400 credits), and another Quarian Log. Accessing the Quarian Log confirms that it was Admiral Rael'Zorah's intention to take back the homeworld. Just beyond the room is Admiral Rael'Zorah's dead body. Tali tries to convince herself that her father isn't dead. Shepard can comfort Tali with a Paragon interrupt or dialogue choices for morality points. Tali finds a recorded message for her from her father. Rael'Zorah's last words to his daughter are to order her to destroy the main geth hub and to bring the data to Admirals Xen and Gerrel. In the room to the left beside Rael'Zorah is a med\-kit, a Wall Safe (\+1500 credits) that can be bypassed, a second Wall Safe (\+2700 credits) that can be bypassed, and some power cells. **Tip:** If you're already full on heavy weapon ammo, you can save the power cells for after the final battle as you'll be able to return here. Also save your game at this point before opening the door at the top of the stairs as the final battle will again be close\-quarters combat and the door locks behind you until the fight is done. Up the stairs from Admiral Rael'Zorah's body is the final battle of the mission: a Geth Prime, a Geth Hunter, and two Geth Troopers. The geth will have their backs turned towards the squad, so Shepard has the element of surprise. In between Shepard and the geth is an unbreakable glass wall. Though the geth can be seen, they cannot be targeted by powers through the glass wall. **Combat Strategy:** One very effective tactic is to put your squadmates into cover behind each of the two desks at the entrance. Then, move slightly around the corner and knock down (using powers or your weapons) the shield of one of the smaller geth, and immediately hit it with Tali's AI Hacking power. Most of the geth will immediately begin fighting amongst themselves; when one slips through toward you, usually the Geth Hunter first, then you'll be able to concentrate on just that one with your entire squad. Meanwhile you can repeat this tactic whenever the hack ends (or a hacked geth is killed) to keep the geth fighting among themselves. Eventually you will be left with just the Geth Prime, and will be able to deal with it without worrying about getting flanked or surrounded \-\- you can just keep falling back in circles whenever you are too hard\-pressed. **Note:**  If you have the M\-920 Cain while encountering the Geth Prime, you can fire it to the furthest wall to kill all of the geth on the bridge immediately. Shooting any closer may result in your death as well. Before getting the evidence from the console at the back of the room, Shepard should pick a Quarian Model Ship for the model ship collection, and access a laptop (\+3000 credits). The evidence console contains recordings revealing that Rael'Zorah was deliberately reactivating geth and linking them in neural networks to reach sapience in order to perform weapons tests on them. However, Rael makes it clear that Tali has no knowledge of his criminal activities. Despite the likelihood of this evidence exonerating her, Tali begs Shepard not to reveal it at her trial to preserve her father's name, as his actions violated laws so "sacred" to the quarian people that he would be viewed as a traitor for all time. Once Shepard uses the console the team automatically returns to the Rayya.

After Tali'Zorah vas Neema is accused of treason against the quarian people, Admiral Xen is one of the three admirals present as judges, along with fellow admirals Zaal'Koris vas Qwib Qwib and Han'Gerrel vas Neema. She is described by Han'Gerrel as being on the fence regarding Tali's treason and refers to the trial as "a farce born of fear." Xen describes Zaal'Koris as a coward and Han'Gerrel as "an aging warship". She sees Han'Gerrel's plans for war with the geth as foolish and self\-destructive, but she has no qualms about experimenting on active geth. Her reasoning is that they are just machines which were created with the sole purpose of serving their creators. If Commander Shepard brought Legion along to the Migrant Fleet, Xen finds it fascinating, originally assuming it to be a simple mech built with a geth shell, more so that it chose a name. She wistfully mutters about the things she could learn "under slightly different circumstances", to which Legion responds that it is not available for experimentation. Furthermore, Legion describes her plans for controlling the geth as "unsound" — a statement with which Tali'Zorah agrees. After the conclusion of Tali's trial, Admiral Xen sends a message to Shepard's terminal that she did some searching of her own aboard the Alarei. She cryptically states that had Shepard presented the results of Rael'Zorah's research, humanity would've reaped the benefits. Instead, they "will watch from a distance as the quarian people reclaim not just their homeworld, but the largest synthetic army in the galaxy." If Tali's father is outed during the trial, Xen (if spoken to) chastises Shepard for revealing the nature of Rael's work in public. evidence.text:
Admiral Daro'Xen vas Moreh was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board known for her clinical intellect and keen scientific interest in the geth, whom she regarded as machines built solely to serve their creators. She was said to have performed surgery on her childhood toys without guilt. She wished to return the geth to quarian control.

In Mass Effect 2, Xen was one of three admirals judging Tali'Zorah's treason trial, alongside Zaal'Koris vas Qwib Qwib and Han'Gerrel vas Neema. She viewed the trial as "a farce born of fear," called Zaal'Koris a coward and Han'Gerrel "an aging warship," and considered war with the geth foolish, though she had no qualms about experimenting on active geth. If Shepard brought Legion, she found it fascinating and mused about experimenting on it, prompting Legion to state it was not available and to call her control plans "unsound," a view Tali shared. Afterward she messaged Shepard that had Rael'Zorah's research been presented, humanity would have benefited; instead the quarians would reclaim their homeworld and the largest synthetic army in the galaxy.

In Mass Effect 3, Xen's research and development corps created white-noise jamming against geth ladar systems, prompting the Admiralty to vote for war, and she led the Special Projects group. If Tali was absent, Xen provided electronic support during the mission to disable a geth dreadnought, gave Shepard a prototype Arc Pistol, and later left in a geth fighter. She created the Sync Laser marking technology that cut through geth jamming, critical to the assault on the Reaper base on Rannoch. She repeatedly expressed interest in dissecting Legion or the Geth VI, argued with Tali over search-and-rescue versus salvage priorities, and briefed Shepard on the rescue of Admiral Koris. If she survived the geth-quarian war, she was sent to help build the Crucible, where Shala'Raan vas Tonbay described her as dissatisfied with the device but lending her technical skills. She was voiced by Claudia Black.

evidence.text:
Admiral Han'Gerrel vas Neema was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board and commander of the Heavy Fleet. He had a long history of provoking trouble along the turian border. A committed advocate of reclaiming the quarian homeworld, he argued that the Migrant Fleet had the largest fleet in the galaxy yet did nothing with it; Tali'Zorah countered that the ships might be needed against the Reapers, and he replied the quarians would need a homeworld to shelter non-combatants. Daro'Xen vas Moreh derisively called him "an aging warship," and he in turn dismissed Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib Qwib as a "whining suit-wetter."

Han'Gerrel was a friend of Tali's father, Rael'Zorah, having served with him aboard the gunship Yaska before their Pilgrimage. During a batarian raid that killed six of ten crew, the two, left alone on the bridge and under orders to hold position, disobeyed to recover a tramp freighter; they received medals and were sent on Pilgrimage early. During Tali's treason trial on the Migrant Fleet, Han'Gerrel sympathized with her and believed her innocent. He was the one person Shepard and Tali could confide in about the nature of Rael's experiments on the Alarei; despite his pro-war stance the experiments horrified him, and he vowed to keep the truth quiet to protect what Rael had wanted for the fleet.

Han'Gerrel was among the admirals who pushed for war against the geth, driving the synthetics to ally with the Reapers and trapping the Migrant Fleet within the Perseus Veil. When Shepard helped disable a geth dreadnought, Han'Gerrel ordered the fleet to press the attack on the geth flagship while Shepard's squad was still aboard. Back on the Normandy, Hackett and Shala'Raan condemned his recklessness, Raan threatening a treason charge. Shepard could hear his explanation or punch him and send him off the ship. He later clashed with Raan over comm about fleet maneuvering. After the Reaper controlling the geth was destroyed, Han'Gerrel ordered an all-out attack on the disabled geth fleet; whether he broke off depended on Shepard having earned the quarians' trust, and if not, the assault destroyed the entire Migrant Fleet.

evidence.page: Tali'Zorah vas Normandy — Character Analysis (Part 4) — Mass Effect 3 and Rannoch
evidence.text:
The fourth part of a hand-corrected video-essay character analysis covered Tali'Zorah in Mass Effect 3. If she survived the Suicide Mission, she apologized to Shepard for the trial and admitted he had been right: "I was too ready to sacrifice myself for the good of the Fleet. I need to stop doing that." She took an Admiral's seat in her father's place specifically to push back against the Board's worst ideas, the version of Tali the essayist preferred. If exiled, she instead told Shepard the trial had shown her she belonged "on the Normandy, helping you," aiding her people from the shadows.

As Admiral she doubted her fitness to command, with seventeen million lives riding on her. After speaking with Legion she believed the quarians could sue for peace, but once Daro'Xen turned Rael'Zorah's research into "an invasion too good to pass up," Tali had no choice but to support it "for the good of the Fleet," regressing toward the sacrificial lamb of ME2 and becoming a near-powerless victim of politics again. The essay noted quarian scarcity: 17 million in the flotilla, one child per family unless the population declines, every quarian contributing to the Fleet's survival. Shala'Raan was the reason Tali was permitted to attempt to retake the Alarei.

At the Rannoch climax Shepard chose between peace, geth genocide, or quarian genocide. Siding with the quarians, Tali killed Legion (or shut the geth down) with a "flat shovel blade," expressed regret, and answered Legion's last question, "Does this unit have a soul?", with "Yes... yes, it does." Siding with the geth, Tali begged Shepard not to choose them over her people, then as Admiral called off the quarian fleet's attack while Legion sacrificed himself to disseminate the code. On the botched path, unable to stop Han'Gerrel, Rael and Daro'Xen, Tali watched what remained of the quarian fleet burn in Rannoch's atmosphere, Captain Ysra of the Rayya on the radio, and took her own life before her home ship burned. Afterward, if the geth helped rebuild Rannoch, Tali admitted: "I'd have killed the geth with no regrets, and I'd have been wrong."

evidence.text:
Ice Giant was the opening mission of Mass Effect: Infiltrator, serving as the game's tutorial for cover, aiming, and powers. Cerberus Infiltrator Randall Ezno was deployed by shuttle to an unnamed ice planet to capture a high-value turian target. His handler and technician, Inali Renata, briefed and guided him over comms, and the operation doubled as a live field test of Randall's newest augmentations.

The mission ran across four checkpoints. Randall fought through geth opposition including Geth Troopers, Geth Juggernauts, and a Turian Sniper, using cover, Pull, Push, Cloak, Charge, and Slide to raise his Combat Analysis Style and Health ratings. Inali repeatedly coached him to stay in cover; Randall answered sarcastically ("Gee, ya think?"). When Inali noted he carried more implants than any other subject, Randall replied, "Well, more than any human subject," alluding to Cerberus's other experiments.

At the fourth checkpoint Randall defeated the turian target, who tended to flee behind cover and required longer-range weapons and powers to finish. After the fight Randall chose how to handle the capture, then dragged the turian back to the shuttle and returned to the Cerberus home base, the Barn. The captured turian later attempted to escape during Randall's disruption of the Cerberus base, and became the protagonist of Infiltrator's bonus mission, Incarceration.

evidence.text:
Matriarch Aethyta was an asari who worked as a bartender in the Eternity lounge on Illium. In Mass Effect 2 she told Commander Shepard how she came to that job despite being a matriarch. Her father was a krogan who fought in the Rachni Wars and Krogan Rebellions, and her mother was an asari commando who also fought in the Rebellions. When her parents learned they had once been enemies during the Rebellions, they fought a duel that neither survived; Aethyta was then about a hundred years old and an exotic dancer. She later took many mates, including a turian, an elcor, and a hanar, and fathered a pureblood daughter she lost track of.

Aethyta held unconventional, free-spirited views. She supported the asari becoming more militant and active in galactic affairs and believed young asari should improve society during their maiden years rather than becoming strippers or mercenaries. Her proposal that the asari build new mass relays was ridiculed, prompting her to leave Thessia for Illium. Shepard met her while she fended off Conrad Verner, who was trying to obtain the deed to her bar on behalf of an "undercover cop" who claimed the place was a front for red sand dealers.

In Mass Effect 3, Aethyta appeared at Apollo's Cafe in the Presidium Commons. She confirmed she was Liara T'Soni's "father" and was watching Liara on behalf of other matriarchs, who were suspicious of Liara's work as an information broker, her ties to Matriarch Benezia, and her friendship with the formerly Cerberus-affiliated Shepard. She warned that the matriarchs might order a hit on Liara. If Shepard was friendly toward Liara, Aethyta was amused to hear Shepard echo her "nobody messes with my girl" line and conceded Shepard might be good enough for her daughter. If Shepard arranged for the two to talk, they discussed the matriarchs' spying, asari war doctrine, Liara's krogan grandfather, and Aethyta's century-long relationship with Benezia, whom Aethyta implied she had married and still loved. Reconciled, Aethyta sent asari mercenaries to aid the war effort.

evidence.text: Aethyta is willing to discuss her life with Commander Shepard and how she ended up as a bartender despite being an asari matriarch. She explains that her father was a krogan who fought in the Rachni Wars and Krogan Rebellions, while her mother was an asari commando who also fought in the Rebellions. Her mother kept her commando leathers for "special nights" with her father, and her father always showed off his war scars and talked about how he stomped a Rachni Queen to death on some poisonous world. When Aethyta's father learned that he and Aethyta's mother were once mortal enemies during the Krogan Rebellions, they decided to fight, a battle neither of them survived. During this time Aethyta was about a hundred years old and an exotic dancer. For the rest of her lifespan, she had many mates, including a turian, elcor, and a hanar. She also fathered a pureblood daughter, but her relationship with the mother didn't work out, and Aethyta lost track of her daughter. Aethyta has very different views on matters than other matriarchs and a very free\-spirited, laissez\-faire attitude to life. She seems to support the asari becoming more militant and active on the galactic stage, and believes that young asari should help improve society in their maiden years instead of becoming strippers or mercenaries. Her proposal that the asari should try to construct new mass relays was met with ridicule, causing the other asari to "laugh the blue off \[her] ass". Realizing that no one wanted to listen to her arguments, Aethyta left Thessia for a less conventional matriarch's life on Illium. Shepard meets Aethyta while she is trying to fend off Conrad Verner, who is trying to get the deed to the place on behest of an "undercover cop". She is trying very hard not to "slap \[Conrad's] ass with a Singularity", until she is rescued by Shepard's arrival. When Conrad explains that the "cop" told him the place is a front for red sand dealers, Aethyta tells him that her bar doesn't sell red sand\-\-and besides, it is legal on Illium as long as the seller has a permit. Shepard can pursue the matter with Conrad. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: Since leaving their homeworld and realising they could mate with any species, an attitude has developed among asari that mating with other races gives greater insight into that particular species. Therefore, mating with other races has become the preferred option, since it has an evolving effect on the resulting offspring, and therefore on the asari race itself. "Pureblooded" asari on the other hand, who have two asari parents, are seen as wasteful by some because "nothing has been gained". However, it is considered cruel and insulting to say such a thing to a pureblooded asari's face. Liara T'Soni talks about herself as a possible pureblood in discussions with Commander Shepard. She mentions that her mother, Matriarch Benezia, never mentioned who her father was, but Liara claims to know that her "second parent" was another asari. This was mostly speculation on Liara's part as an explanation for Benezia's silence, but it was not unjustified, as this was something Benezia would have preferred to keep secret as to avoid the public humiliation. Liara clearly found discussing her parentage quite painful, but she has wondered about the identity of her "father" and what happened between her parents. She does discover that her "father" is indeed another asari. Ardat\-Yakshi are asari born with a rare genetic defect that renders them unable to properly meld with the nervous systems of others, which in its most severe form is lethal to anyone they mate with. Ardat\-Yakshi can only be purebloods, which the justicar Samara, a pureblood herself, theorizes is the origin of the stigma against purebloods. Samara herself has three daughters, all of whom are Ardat\-Yakshi: Morinth, Rila, and Falere.

evidence.text: *For her gameplay attributes in Mass Effect 3, see Squad Members Guide (Mass Effect 3\)\#Liara T'Soni.* “Well, I suppose I did just write your name in the stars.” Liara has taken over the Shadow Broker's operations regardless of Shepard's involvement. Unfortunately, the Reaper invasion hit Earth. During the chaos, Cerberus assaults the Archives and Liara finds herself evading their troops through the air ducts. Through her Shadow Broker network, Liara greatly aids the war effort against the Reapers by acquiring intelligence, contacts, munitions, military forces, and other crucial resources. When Shepard first comes to Liara's office after the meeting with the Council, she's talking to Joker about the "less than ideal" outcome of the meeting. evidence.text:
"Pureblood" was a term for the child of two asari parents. It was considered negatively charged and offensive, arising from asari biology and outlook. After leaving their homeworld and realising they could reproduce with any species, asari developed the view that mating with other races granted greater insight into that species and had an evolving effect on their offspring and thus the asari race itself. Pureblooded asari, by contrast, were seen by some as wasteful because "nothing has been gained," though saying so to a pureblood's face was regarded as cruel and insulting.

Liara T'Soni discussed her own possible pureblood status with Commander Shepard. Her mother, Matriarch Benezia, never named Liara's other parent; Liara believed her "second parent" was another asari, which she treated as an explanation for Benezia's silence and the public humiliation Benezia would have wished to avoid. Liara found the topic painful and wondered about the identity of her "father." She does eventually discover that her other parent was indeed another asari.

Ardat-Yakshi were asari born with a rare genetic defect preventing them from properly melding with others' nervous systems; in its most severe form it killed anyone they mated with. Ardat-Yakshi could only be purebloods, which the justicar Samara, herself a pureblood, theorized was the origin of the stigma against purebloods. Samara had three daughters, all Ardat-Yakshi: Morinth, Rila and Falere.

evidence.text:
Irikah Krios was the wife of the drell assassin Thane Krios and the mother of Kolyat Krios, remembered for her sunset-colored eyes. As told in Mass Effect: Foundation, she was a lab researcher working on a vaccine for a rare hanar disease, work that drew "moral objections"; thugs broke into her lab and Thane intervened to help her fight them off, though she handled one attacker herself. Earlier she had prevented an assassination of an elderly salarian in a park by stepping into the targeting laser's path. Learning it was Thane behind the trigger, she began to call security but changed her mind on hearing his plea for redemption.

Despite her skepticism and contempt, she showed Thane compassion and eventually forgave him. They grew close, dated, and married in a small open-air ceremony. Irikah told Thane he was free to choose his own future, advice he heeded by asking the hanar to release him from his Compact. She gave him a coin that had belonged to her father, saying that rubbing it had brought her father peace of mind. After Kolyat was born and money was tight, she supported Thane's decision to freelance as an assassin.

One of Thane's jobs, killing the leaders of a batarian slaver ring, brought vengeful batarians down on the family; too afraid to target Thane directly, they paid the Shadow Broker to identify him and sent a hitman after his home. Sensing intruders, Irikah told Kolyat to hide and armed herself with a knife, but was killed. Thane returned to Kahje for her funeral, left Kolyat with relatives, and hunted down those complicit in her murder, letting them suffer before they died. He later threw her father's coin into the sea. By 2185 her memory formed much of the backstory Thane shares with Commander Shepard after his recruitment on Illium; she had reminded him of Arashu, the goddess of motherhood and protection.

evidence.text:
Dr. Alestia Iallis was an asari molecular geneticist educated at the University of Auräis and later stationed at Peak 15 on Noveria. She specialized in biotic-enhanced allele-specific hybridization, tracking inherited variations in genetic sequences. Records indicated she had been transferred to Peak 15 about a month earlier at the behest of an investor, Saren Arterius.

Commander Shepard first met Alestia with the science team at Rift Station. She was oddly calm about the crisis and pointedly rude, accusing Shepard of interrupting her meditations. Asked about Matriarch Benezia, she claimed to know her no better than Shepard knew Earth's President Huerta, and suggested Shepard ask Liara instead if she was present.

If Shepard agreed to help Dr. Zev Cohen develop a cure for scientists sickened by a biotoxin, one of Captain Ventralis's guards let the squad into the quarantined lab and locked them in until they could be scanned clean. Once the cure was made, Alestia ambushed the squad with a group of geth, revealing herself as an asari commando under orders from Benezia to kill Shepard at the first opportunity and expressing delight that the squad was trapped for quiet disposal. Alestia and her team were killed in the ensuing fight. Afterward the squad found the murdered guard outside the lab and confronted Dr. Cohen, who insisted he had been unaware that Alestia was a commando. If a firefight broke out with Rift Station's guards before Alestia revealed herself, she simply disappeared from her post. Alestia was voiced by Shanelle Workman.

evidence.text:
Matriarch Benezia was a very powerful asari biotic and a revered spiritual leader, teacher of religion and philosophy, and the mother of Liara T'Soni, from whom she had been estranged for years. Given her matriarch status she had lived nearly a millennium. During her matron phase she had Liara, unusually mating with another asari, and raised her alone; Liara's study of Prothean archaeology was a minor rebellion against her forward-thinking mother. Benezia believed the asari should have a greater role in shaping galactic events. She was Saren Arterius' executor and a fellow Binary Helix investor. Evidence proving Saren caused the Eden Prime attack also showed Benezia was working alongside him, which shocked those who knew her.

Benezia learned of Saren's plan to aid the Reapers and decided to try to guide him down a less destructive path, giving her followers, including Shiala, the choice to accompany her. The influence of the Reaper Sovereign proved too strong and Benezia became enslaved to Saren's will along with her guards and commandos, serving as something between his advisor and second-in-command. Through Binary Helix she funded a secret project on Noveria to breed rachni from a newly discovered egg for Saren's army; when the brood was removed from the Rachni Queen, the rachni went rogue. Benezia traveled to Peak 15 to investigate and to extract from the Queen's genetic memory the location of the Mu Relay, escorted by asari commandos. She brought geth in crates to guard the garage and left agents such as Alestia Iallis and recruited security including Captain Ventralis to stop Shepard.

Shepard's squad fought through geth, rachni, and commandos to find Benezia beside the Rachni Queen. Using her mental strength to keep part of her mind free of indoctrination, she briefly broke Saren's control, described the horror of indoctrination, gave Shepard the Mu Relay coordinates, and warned of Sovereign's power before turning on the squad, who were forced to kill her. She told Liara her daughter had always made her proud, and as she died claimed not to see the light promised in asari religion. In Mass Effect 3, Benezia's bondmate was revealed to be Matriarch Aethyta; the two had been together for a hundred years before disagreeing over the asari's path. After Thessia revealed a hidden Prothean Beacon, Liara wondered if Benezia knew of the coverup, and EDI suggested Benezia acted to protect Liara.

evidence.text: **Athame** is a hydrogen\-helium gas giant with spectacular rings. The planet's apparent magnitude varies when seen from Thessia based on atmospheric conditions and relative distance. To the ancient asari, the "mysterious star" that shone in some months and disappeared in others was linked to fortune, and so it was named Athame, after the matriarch of the pantheon and a goddess of prophecy and fate. Athame's worship changed over time, eventually becoming the basis for a monotheistic religion in which her maiden, matron and matriarch aspects oversaw all stages and roles in asari society. When an asari says "by the goddess," they are referring to Athame. Like Janiri, the planet Athame served as a rally point during the Reaper invasion, where fleeing asari ships could discharge their drive cores so they could make another FTL jump. The Reapers were forced to chase the asari away from the planet, buying Thessia valuable time.

evidence.text:
The asari, native to the planet Thessia, were often considered the most influential and respected sentient species in the galaxy, known for elegance, diplomacy, and biotic aptitude. They were among the earliest races to achieve interstellar flight after the Protheans and the first to discover and settle the Citadel, and they were instrumental in proposing and founding the Citadel Council.

A mono-gendered race with a feminine appearance and a roughly thousand-year lifespan, asari could reproduce with a partner of any gender or species through a process of parthenogenesis. During "melding" (the joining or union), an asari attuned her nervous system to her partner's to randomize her offspring's second gene set; offspring were always asari regardless of the partner's species. Melding could also be used purely to share thoughts, as when Liara T'Soni melded with Commander Shepard to interpret the Prothean beacon visions and Shiala uploaded the Cipher into Shepard's mind. The Ardat-Yakshi were asari with a rare genetic defect that destroyed a partner's nervous system during joining, appearing almost exclusively among "purebloods" born of two asari parents, a status considered a grave insult. Asari passed through three life stages: Maiden (from puberty, marked by exploration), Matron (around age 350, a desire to settle and raise children), and Matriarch (around age 700, acting as community sages and councilors).

Asari civilization on Thessia was secretly accelerated by the Protheans, who posed as the goddess Athame with guides Janiri and Lucen, genetically enhanced asari biotics, and left a beacon containing the VI Vendetta in what became the Temple of Athame; this was a closely held state secret. The asari found the Citadel in 580 BCE with the aid of the keepers, and with the salarians founded the Council in 500 BCE. During the 2186 Reaper invasion the asari initially withheld support, but after the Reapers overwhelmed their defenses their government revealed the Prothean beacon to Shepard; Thessia fell, and the asari finally committed forces to the Allied war effort.

Asari culture favored the "long view," centrism, consensus, and cultural domination over conflict. Their government, the Asari Republics, functioned as an inclusive electronic democracy deferring to Matriarchs. Their mainstream religion was siari ("All is one"), alongside worship of Athame. The asari military resembled tribal warrior bands of full-time professionals, favoring commando huntresses skilled in ambush, infiltration, and assassination, and fielding one of the galaxy's most powerful navies, including the dreadnought Destiny Ascension. Some asari became justicars, adherents of an ancient code.
